provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Pro family batch. Regulated: copy never promises a refund, a saving or an outcome, and never gives tax advice. Credentials appear only as bracketed placeholders. No software or payroll vendor names. Ranges are planning figures.

pageStructurePlus.section: Tax season calendar and intake cut-off
pageStructurePlus.contains: Filing deadlines for individuals and businesses, quarterly estimate dates, extension cut-offs, and the date the practice stops taking new tax returns for the season
pageStructurePlus.why: Tax clients decide inside a narrow window. A visible intake cut-off turns 'I'll call in March' into a booked January appointment.

pageStructurePlus.section: Tax document checklist and secure upload
pageStructurePlus.contains: Printable checklists for wage earners, sole proprietors, landlords and small businesses, a secure upload link, and a plain note on what never to send by email
pageStructurePlus.why: 'What do I bring?' is the first question a new tax client has. A checklist answers it at 11pm and makes the first meeting short.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How months or years of behind books get reconciled, which bank and card statements are needed, how cleanup is quoted, and what a closed set of books looks like at the end
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners who are behind feel embarrassed and wait. A calm cleanup page with no judgement is what gets them to call before the deadline does.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Short pages for contractors, restaurants, salons, landlords and online sellers covering job costing, tips, sales tax, rental schedules and inventory, in plain words
pageStructurePlus.why: A contractor wants a bookkeeper who already knows job costing. Industry pages let each owner see their own kind of business before they book.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What to do when a tax notice arrives, how to send a copy securely, how quickly the office responds, and who may represent clients [EA or CPA credential, if held]
pageStructurePlus.why: A notice in the mailbox is the most urgent moment a tax client has, and it is often when they switch preparers. This page catches that search.

designDirections.name: Ledger Ready
designDirections.bestFor: Solo preparers and one-person bookkeeping offices who mostly need the phone and the tax appointment request to work
designDirections.headlineSample: Bookkeeping and tax prep for {City} owners and families
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a neutral grotesque read like a clean invoice. One appointment button, the checklist and the intake cut-off, nothing else competing.

designDirections.name: Year-Round Books
designDirections.bestFor: Bookkeeping practices with monthly clients and a tax season, who want consultations booked and documents uploaded without phone tag
designDirections.headlineSample: Monthly books and tax returns, handled all year in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's Private Vault combo. A warm cream ground and a refined serif feel like a private office, which is what someone handing over bank statements needs to see.

designDirections.name: Counting House
designDirections.bestFor: Established tax and bookkeeping firms with enrolled agents or CPAs, advisory clients and a library of plain-language guides
designDirections.headlineSample: A {City} tax and bookkeeping practice, open all twelve months
designDirections.whyItFits: A bookish serif and an accounting-ledger palette suit a firm that wins on long explanations and years of practice, not on a bold offer.

openers.line: Your Google listing has a phone number and hours but no website, so someone choosing a tax preparer can't see who you help or what a return costs before they call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what could sit behind that button for a tax practice: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens a Facebook page. A business owner handing over a year of bank statements wants a private office page and a secure way to send them, not a feed of tax reminders.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the latest deadline reminder they posted.
openers.linkLine: A bookkeeping page built for the client, not the feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site linked from your listing still carries a free-host banner and last season's tax deadlines. People trusting you with their return notice the stale dates first.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for an old copyright year, last year's filing dates or a dead form. Note which one you found.
openers.linkLine: The same tax practice, current and quick on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Hard to read on a phone
openers.line: I opened your bookkeeping site on my phone and the services ran off the side of the screen. Most owners look for a bookkeeper on their phone after closing up for the night.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks: menu, fee table or contact form. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your bookkeeping site rebuilt for a phone at night: {demo-link}

openers.angle: No way to book or upload
openers.line: There's no way to book a tax appointment or send documents except calling and dropping off a folder. A lot of new clients would rather pick a slot and upload their wage forms at 10pm.
openers.hook: Check the listing, social pages and any site for a booking link or upload. If there's neither, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A tax appointment and secure upload in one place: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews mention a preparer who explained everything and answered a panicked text in April. That reassurance never reaches anyone who isn't already on your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about calm, clarity or being explained to. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those tax client reviews next to the services they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Tax season intake starts the week the wage forms arrive. The bookkeeper with an appointment page and a checklist already up books January while everyone else is still returning voicemails.
openers.hook: Use this from October to early January. Name the month in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the first wage forms land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Small business owners think about their bookkeeping after the shop closes. When the only option is calling an office that shut at five, the question waits until next quarter.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it goes to a generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A bookkeeping enquiry that works after hours: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a seasonal tax preparer. Good preparers check whether a practice looks established before they commit a whole tax season to it.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a job listing. Note the date of the post.
openers.linkLine: A tax practice page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts mention bookkeeping clients outside {City}. A site that says you work remotely, with secure upload and video meetings, is what an owner two towns over types in.
openers.hook: Look for mentions of virtual meetings, other towns or out-of-state clients. Use the town furthest from their office.
openers.linkLine: Bookkeeping pages for clients near and far: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing on your profile says what a tax return or monthly bookkeeping costs. People don't need an exact price, but a genuine starting range is what gets them to book instead of shopping three preparers.
openers.hook: Check every profile for a price or a 'starting at'. If there's none anywhere, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Bookkeeping and tax fees shown as honest ranges: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your credentials appear in a post from last year but nowhere a new tax client would look. Showing the preparer credential, the office address and the privacy policy is the first thing that separates a real practice from a pop-up.
openers.hook: Look for any credential they've published themselves. Never quote a number or credential they haven't posted.
openers.linkLine: Credentials, privacy and fees on one tax practice page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your bookkeeping clients come from other clients. That works until the referrer retires, and even a referred owner searches your name before handing over their books.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'my friend recommended' or 'been with them for years'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred bookkeeping client would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Tax notices go out in waves through the summer, and people search for help the day one arrives. A page that says what to send you and how fast you respond would catch those calls.
openers.hook: Use this from May to September. Check whether they mention notices or audits anywhere.
openers.linkLine: A tax notice help page for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted about was a clear explanation of a tax deadline. A post like that should live on a bookkeeping site where it keeps working, not disappear down a feed.
openers.hook: Pick their newest helpful post, a deadline reminder or a tip, and name it exactly.
openers.linkLine: That tax tip, kept on a page that ranks: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted was a clear, useful tax reminder.

I looked for bookkeeping and tax prep in {City} and found {Business Name} on social, but no site with your fees, a document checklist and a way to book. I put together a sample page to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my note got buried under client emails. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a tax appointment request, a printable document checklist, a cleanup bookkeeping page and a spot for your credentials and privacy policy. If it's not for you, just say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for bookkeepers and tax preparers here in {City}. I sent you a message a few days ago, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"No problem, inboxes are brutal this time of year. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with appointment booking, a document checklist and secure upload, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link to look at this evening?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"This isn't marketing or ads, it's a site you own. The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many industry pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and updates like new deadlines. For a practice your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is roughly what a couple of monthly bookkeeping clients bring in."
"Could I walk you through it for ten minutes, before the season starts?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. Once it clears we start, and it's live before the wage forms go out."

objections.objection: All my clients come from referrals.
objections.handler: "That's the best kind. A referred owner still searches your name before handing over their books. The site is what they find, and it's where you send them the checklist."

objections.objection: It's tax season, I can't think about this until May.
objections.handler: "Completely fair. Let's book a call for the week after the deadline, and it's built through the summer so it's ready for next January."

objections.objection: My accounting software gives me a free page already.
objections.handler: "Those pages are fine for a listing, but they belong to the vendor and look like every other practice. Your own domain carries your fees, your checklist and your name, and it moves with you."

objections.objection: I'm full. I don't want more tax clients.
objections.handler: "Then the site does a different job: fewer phone calls, documents uploaded instead of dropped off, and a waitlist for monthly bookkeeping clients you'd actually choose."

objections.objection: I can't put prices on a website. Every return is different.
objections.handler: "Nobody expects a fixed price. A 'returns from' range and how you quote cleanup work filters out the shoppers before they take your time."
"{Build Range}. For you I'd quote about {Build Price}, for booking, the checklist, upload and a few industry pages. That's less than one small business client pays you in a quarter."

email.subject: Tax practice site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for bookkeepers and tax preparers in {City}, and I made a sample one for {Business Name} with booking and a document checklist. I'll email the link. Have a look when the day's returns are done. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} tax practice demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to keep it up? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, the wage forms go out in a few weeks and the January calls are about to start. You came to mind.

The bookkeeping and tax site is still here whenever you want it, same price as before. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a couple of monthly bookkeeping clients, never to an hourly rate. Practices think in recurring clients.
Sell between May and November. From January to mid-April nobody in a tax office answers a sales call.
Price secure upload and booking as their own lines; they replace a front-desk job and that's how the owner values them.
Industry pages are separate lines, each one quoted only for an industry they already serve.
Keep fee pages as ranges the owner approves. Never write a promised refund or saving into any copy.
Quote a Spanish-language tax path only where they already prepare returns in Spanish.

lineItems.item: Tax appointment booking with intake questions
lineItems.description: Max with separate paths for individuals, sole proprietors and businesses, a prior-preparer question and reminder texts.
Max when uploads are sorted by client and tax year, with a confirmation email and a checklist that ticks off what arrived.
Max when the page has its own FAQ, an example monthly report layout and a short case note the owner approves.
Max with months-behind and account-count questions that route to a rough quote range the owner sets.

lineItems.item: Tax deadline calendar with switchable banners
lineItems.description: Max when the banner changes on its own for intake open, the cut-off, extensions and quarterly estimates.
Max when the checklist, fees, booking and privacy policy are all translated and reviewed by the owner.

lineItems.item: Tax notice help page with secure send
lineItems.description: Max with an upload form just for notices and an urgent flag that texts the owner.

whatElseYouSell.name: Office and headshot photo session
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One morning of headshots for each preparer and a few shots of the office gives the bookkeeping site real faces. People hand their tax return to a person, not a logo."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, before the next tax season opens.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts on tax deadlines
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every deadline, extension date and intake cut-off goes on your Google profile the week it matters, so the listing looks like an active tax office, not a dormant one."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each return is filed
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day a tax return is filed, the client gets a short text asking how it went. Reviews written in April are the ones January searchers read."

whatElseYouSell.name: January return-client reminder campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every past tax client gets an email and a text in early January with the checklist and a booking link, before another preparer's flyer reaches them."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in November, send in early January.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly small business tax newsletter
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short monthly email to bookkeeping clients and prospects: upcoming deadlines, one plain explainer and a reminder to send receipts. General information only, written for you to approve."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the client list is in one place.

whatElseYouSell.name: Referral pack for bankers and attorneys
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page leave-behind and a matching landing page for the business bankers and estate attorneys who send you bookkeeping clients, so their referral lands somewhere clear."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, when they name who refers to them.

whatElseYouSell.name: LinkedIn profile refresh for the preparers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Business owners check a bookkeeper's LinkedIn before a meeting. I rewrite the headline and summary so they match the practice site and the industries you serve."

whatElseYouSell.name: Chamber and networking one-pager
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printed one-pager for chamber breakfasts and networking groups that says who your bookkeeping practice helps, the fee ranges and where to book."
whatElseYouSell.when: Any time they mention a networking group.

withoutAI.route: The bookkeeper's own small business clients
withoutAI.whoPays: Each client business, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "You see which of your bookkeeping clients have no website or a broken one. An introduction from their bookkeeper is the warmest door I'll ever get."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: The bookkeeper sees every client's books and knows who is growing. Their word carries more weight than any cold message.

withoutAI.route: Independent financial advisors they refer to
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The advisors you send tax clients to need a consultation site as much as you did. Your introduction gets me past their front desk."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Advisors and preparers trade clients every spring, and an advisor buys a site on the same logic: credentials first, then a booked meeting.

withoutAI.route: Estate planning attorneys who share clients
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When a tax client asks about a will or a trust, you send them to someone. That attorney needs a careful site and you can make the introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Estate attorneys rely on referrals from preparers and treat a referral partner's recommendation seriously.

withoutAI.route: Small landlords from the rental schedules
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your clients with rental schedules need a simple listing and tenant request page. I build it, and the bookkeeping for those rentals stays with you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landlords with a handful of doors have a real problem and already trust the person who does their tax return.

withoutAI.route: Independent insurance agents in the same building
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The insurance agent who shares your business clients has a dull carrier page. A bookkeeper's introduction makes that rebuild an easy talk."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents and preparers serve the same owners and often share referrals and office parks.

withoutAI.route: New business owners from the formation consults
withoutAI.whoPays: The new business, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every owner you help set up new bookkeeping for needs a website in the same month they open a bank account. You can mention me in the same meeting."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: New owners are buying everything at once and trust the bookkeeper who set up their books.

withAI.route: Receipt sorting assistant for client businesses
withAI.pitchLine: "Your bookkeeping clients snap receipts into a text thread and an assistant sorts them by category and month before they reach you."
withAI.whyItWorks: The bookkeeper gets cleaner inputs and the client pays for the convenience, so the bookkeeper happily recommends it.

withAI.route: Meeting summary drafts for financial advisors
withAI.pitchLine: "Advisors you refer tax clients to write meeting notes at night. An assistant drafts the summary and the follow-up list for them to check."
withAI.whyItWorks: Advisors bill for meetings, not notes. A tool that returns evenings sells on the first week.

withAI.route: Intake questionnaire assistant for estate attorneys
withAI.pitchLine: "Estate attorneys spend the first meeting gathering facts. An assistant walks the client through the family, asset and tax questions beforehand and drafts a fact sheet for the attorney."
withAI.whyItWorks: It saves billable time on intake, and the preparer's introduction lands the first demo.

withAI.route: Tenant question bot for small landlords
withAI.pitchLine: "Your landlord clients answer the same tenant questions every week. A small assistant answers rent, parking and repair questions from their own house rules."
withAI.whyItWorks: Landlords with a few doors can't afford a manager but will pay a small monthly fee to stop the texts.

withAI.route: Policy renewal reminder assistant for insurance agents
withAI.pitchLine: "The insurance agent who shares your bookkeeping clients loses renewals to silence. An assistant drafts renewal check-ins for each policy and books a review call."
withAI.whyItWorks: Renewals are the agent's income. Fewer quiet lapses pays for the tool in one saved account.

withAI.route: Startup paperwork guide for new business owners
withAI.pitchLine: "New owners from your formation consults get a guided checklist of registrations, accounts and records to keep, with general information only and a link back to your bookkeeping."
withAI.whyItWorks: Owners pay for a clear path in a confusing month, and every finished checklist points back to the bookkeeper.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for tax season
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every call you miss while you're with a tax client gets a text with the booking link and the document checklist. Half the callback is done before you pick up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their business number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Document checklist portal with missing-item list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each tax client gets their own checklist from last year's return, ticks off what they've uploaded, and sees exactly what's still missing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: November, before intake opens. Needs their checklist by client type and the upload method they already trust.

softwareAI.name: Engagement letter and fee sign-off at booking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a new bookkeeping client books, the engagement letter and fee schedule go out for e-signature automatically, so nobody starts work without one."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their current engagement letter, fee schedule and the signing tool they use.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts in the preparer's voice
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review of your tax practice gets a reply drafted in your voice that thanks them without mentioning anything confidential, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Needs ten of their past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer, and never names a client's tax details.

softwareAI.name: Tax appointment scheduler across preparers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each preparer's calendar shows real tax appointment slots by return type, so a simple return doesn't take a two-hour business slot in March."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: December. Needs each preparer's hours, return types and appointment lengths.

softwareAI.name: Client question assistant on fees, documents and dates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'what do I bring' and 'when's your tax intake cut-off' at midnight from your own pages, gives general information only, and hands anything about a client's own situation to you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their fee ranges, checklist and calendar, updated each season. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Upload sorter for statements and receipts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Bank statements, wage forms and receipts dropped in one pile get sorted by client, tax year and document type before a bookkeeper opens them."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the upload portal. Needs a season of sample uploads and their folder naming rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Monthly close tracker per bookkeeping client
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every bookkeeping client's month on one board: statements received, reconciled, reviewed, report sent. You see who's behind without opening each file."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their close steps and a client list with service level.

softwareAI.name: Missing-document reminder sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A tax client who hasn't uploaded the last statement gets a polite reminder every few days until it arrives, and you stop writing the chase emails by hand."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: January. Needs the checklist portal and the wording they want for each reminder.

softwareAI.name: Online tax organiser questionnaire
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients answer the yearly tax questions about dependants, moves, new jobs and rentals online, and the answers land in their file before the appointment."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: November. Needs their paper organiser and the questions they always ask.

softwareAI.name: Plain-language monthly report notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each bookkeeping client's monthly report comes with a short draft note in plain words on what changed since last month, for you to edit. It describes the numbers, it doesn't advise."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs three months of reports and the notes they'd normally write. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Cleanup bookkeeping scope drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A behind client uploads statements and the tool drafts a cleanup scope, counting months, accounts and transactions, so your quote takes minutes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs several past cleanup jobs and how they priced them. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; the owner sets every final price.

softwareAI.name: Client portal with prior-year returns and invoices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients log in for last year's tax return copy, this year's status and their invoices, instead of calling the office the week their lender asks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs the upload portal and the scheduler in place, plus their file retention rules.

softwareAI.name: Card-on-file billing for monthly bookkeeping
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Monthly bookkeeping fees bill themselves on the first of the month, and tax prep fees bill when the return is ready to sign."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their fee schedule and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Tax notice reader with a response checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A client uploads a tax notice and the tool pulls out the notice type, the dates and the amounts, and drafts a document checklist for the preparer to review."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs past notices with client details removed. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; a credentialed preparer reviews every response.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal tax preparer applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for a seasonal tax preparer seat answer your questions about experience, availability through April and credentials, and you only interview the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: September or October, when they post for the season. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Returns-in-progress board by stage
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every tax return on one board: documents in, prepared, reviewed, waiting on signature, filed. You stop answering 'where is my return' by digging through folders."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: December, before season. Needs their review steps and who signs off.

softwareAI.name: Payroll and sales tax filing calendar per client
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each bookkeeping client's payroll, sales tax and quarterly filing dates in one calendar, with a reminder to the right person the week before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs the client list with filing frequencies by state.

softwareAI.name: Meeting voice notes to engagement memo
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After a new bookkeeping client meeting, talk for two minutes and the tool drafts the scope memo and the engagement letter changes for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs their memo template and engagement letter. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Bookkeeping waitlist and capacity planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the bookkeeping roster is full, new enquiries join a waitlist sorted by industry and size, and the site says so honestly instead of going quiet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they say they're full. Needs a rough count of the hours each client takes.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the tax checklist portal for preparers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a tax document checklist portal for one practice. Every small tax office in the state still chases statements by email."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first practice taught you the workflow and paid for the build. The next office needs only its own checklist.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: State society of tax professionals member kit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member a tax practice site template with booking, a checklist and a privacy page as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need reasons to renew, and members ask them for exactly this help.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Bookkeeping site template for marketing agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency signs accountants and builds each from scratch. License my bookkeeping template with the checklist, cleanup and industry pages finished."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the relationship; you sell them the part you already built and tested.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Small business development centre resource pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The development centre or its host college
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your workshops send new owners to find a bookkeeper. A resource section with plain guides and a vetted local list is the page they keep asking for."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Centres have grant budgets for owner education, and a bookkeeper client is your proof you can explain it plainly.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New business accounts ask the banker for a bookkeeper. A business resources page with vetted local practices keeps that owner banking with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Community banks compete on being local and helpful, and the bookkeeping client becomes the first listed partner.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each tax office needs its own hours, preparers and booking page under one brand. I build the template once and add offices as you open them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many locations, and seasonal offices open and close on a fixed calendar you can plan for.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A switch-on tax season page with booking, a checklist and an intake cut-off, ready for any part-time preparer by the first week of January."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every seasonal preparer needs the same pages at the same time. A kit means no custom build for each.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Spanish-speaking tax preparers in other metros
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The bilingual tax pages I built for one office, with the checklist and privacy policy translated, fit every Spanish-speaking preparer in the region."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Translation and review is the expensive part, and it's already done and checked by a real practice.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Preparers need yearly education hours, and the providers need class pages and sign-ups. Your bookkeeping client knows which providers are good."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Providers sell to every preparer in the state, and a practitioner's referral is the introduction.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fractional finance firm microsites per bookkeeper
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Firms with a bench of contract bookkeepers need a profile and booking page for each one. The template already exists from a working practice."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Each bookkeeper on the bench is a page, so the job grows with their roster.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One tax practice per metro, next city over
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A bookkeeping practice in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one bookkeeping and tax practice per city. {City} is taken; the next metro's best small practice isn't."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusive territory appeals to practices that compete on trust, and the template and demo carry straight over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your tax practice site before last season and stopped answering. I can finish it on a template already live for another practice."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Those owners have already decided to buy and have their copy half written.

upsellLadder.offer: Tax practice site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The bookkeeping site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new deadline banner or fee change is a text to me, not a weekend for you."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests after each return is filed
upsellLadder.trigger: The first new client books through the site and finishes their engagement.
upsellLadder.line: "That new tax client who booked online is exactly who should leave the next review. Let's ask every client the day their return is filed."

upsellLadder.trigger: The bookkeeping site still shows marked placeholders where the preparer photos go.
upsellLadder.line: "Your bookkeeping pages are ready except for faces. One morning of headshots and people can see who they're handing their tax return to."

upsellLadder.offer: Document checklist portal with missing-item list
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of uploads, and they mention chasing clients for the last statement.
upsellLadder.line: "You're chasing statements by email again. Each tax client can see their own checklist and what's still missing."

upsellLadder.trigger: November arrives and they can export last season's client list.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's get the checklist and booking link to every past tax client before another preparer's flyer reaches them."

upsellLadder.offer: Client question assistant on fees, documents and dates
upsellLadder.trigger: The contact form log shows the same fee and checklist questions every week of tax season.
upsellLadder.line: "Half your tax enquiries ask the same three things. The assistant answers those from your own pages and passes the rest to you."

upsellLadder.offer: Monthly close tracker per bookkeeping client
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention hiring a second bookkeeper or a backlog of month-end closes.
upsellLadder.line: "Two bookkeepers and a growing roster won't fit in one spreadsheet. Let's put every client's month on one board."

upsellLadder.offer: Client portal with prior-year returns and invoices
upsellLadder.trigger: Their second tax season on the site, with clients calling for last year's return copies.
upsellLadder.line: "Every lender request means a client calling for last year's tax return. Let them download it themselves."
